name: SELLERS, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that Alabama's "stop and identify" statute, § 15-5-30, empowers officers to demand physical identification when a suspect provides an incomplete or unsatisfactory oral response to verify their identity during a lawful Terry stop.

name: BRYAN, Justice
description: Concurred, agreeing with the main opinion and the sentiments expressed in Justice Shaw's special writing.

name: COOK, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the statute does not prohibit, and in fact authorizes, officers to demand physical identification when oral responses are incomplete or unsatisfactory.

name: SHAW, J.
description: Concurred in the result, arguing that the statute allows officers to demand a person's actual name and address, and does not limit the response to oral answers, thus permitting demands for physical identification if oral responses are nonresponsive.

name: MENDHEIM, Justice
description: Dissented, arguing that the court should have declined to answer the certified question due to principles of comity with federal courts, despite agreeing with the majority's interpretation of the statute.

name: BRYAN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Alabama Workers' Compensation Act is constitutional under both the vested-rights and common-law-rights approaches, and its exclusive-remedy provisions bar the plaintiff's negligence action.

name: Mitchell, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while applying precedents, he is concerned that some precedents conflict with the original public meaning of Article I, § 13, which was intended to guard against corruption of justice, not to freeze common-law remedies.

name: MITCHELL, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that the Wrongful Death of a Minor Act applies to all unborn children, including extrauterine embryos, without exception based on developmental stage or location, and that the Alabama Constitution mandates protection of unborn life.

name: Parker, C.J.
description: Concurred specially, arguing that the Alabama Constitution's declaration of the sanctity of unborn life requires upholding the protection of unborn life, including life outside the womb, and that human life is sacred from conception as made in the image of God.

name: Shaw, J.
description: Concurred specially, arguing that the meaning of 'child' in Alabama law is settled to include unborn children, whether in vitro or in utero, and that prior common-law rules are superseded by the Constitution and statutes.

name: Stewart, J.
description: Concurred, joining Justice Shaw's special concurrence.

name: Mendheim, J.
description: Concurred in the result, agreeing that the Wrongful Death of a Minor Act can be construed to include frozen embryos based on historical judicial expansion, but expressed misgivings about the main opinion's reasoning that the law is 'clear' given IVF's novelty.

name: Sellers, J.
description: Dissented in part, arguing that the Wrongful Death of a Minor Act was not intended to include IVF embryos and that the court is improperly creating a method for punitive damages, while concurring with the dismissal of negligence claims.

name: Cook, J.
description: Dissented, arguing that the court should adhere to the original 1872 meaning of the Wrongful Death Act, which did not cover frozen embryos, and that the decision oversteps the judicial role and will likely end IVF in Alabama.

name: WISE, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the issue of interpreting 'not less than three-fifths of a quorum present' is a nonjusticiable political question, deferring to the legislature's power to determine its own rules.

name: Mitchell, J.
description: Concurred, argued that political questions should lead to dismissal on the merits, not for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction, and that the court should determine if the legislature's interpretation falls within the bounds of its discretion.

name: Parker
description: Concurred in part and concurred in the result, argued that Kelly Walker had standing to challenge the local-tax act's constitutionality under Section 105, and that this claim should have been addressed on its merits, disagreeing with the presumption of constitutionality for Section 105 claims.

name: Mitchell
description: Concurred in part and concurred in the result, argued that the local-tax act does not require distribution to the Gulf Shores Board and that the argument regarding the tax violating Section 105 of the Alabama Constitution, while properly before the court, is without merit.

name: Bryan, J.
description: Concurred, argued that Dixon's regulatory taking claim is not viable under Alabama law, and while he believes the precedent (Town of Gurley) was wrongly decided, it was not asked to be overruled.

name: Wise, J.
description: Concurred with Justice Bryan's special opinion.

name: Mendheim, J.
description: Concurred with Justice Bryan's special opinion.

name: BOLIN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the jury-waiver provision in the PSA is enforceable based on established factors, that Warren Averett's breach made the arbitration provision unenforceable, triggering the jury waiver, and that the motion to strike was not barred by laches.

name: Mitchell, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Gaylord factors for jury-trial waivers are not a definitive test and that the 'buried deep' factor is out of step with contract law, suggesting a revision of the framework in a future case.

name: PARKER, Chief Justice
description: Dissented, argued that jury waivers should be narrowly construed, the arbitration provision was not declared 'unenforceable' as required by the waiver clause, and the majority's decision allows Warren Averett to use its own noncompliance to deprive Fagan of a jury trial, infringing a constitutional right.

name: MITCHELL, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court correctly denied Pinkard's immunity claims and that the previous ruling in Barnhart v. Ingalls, which incorrectly expanded state immunity, should be overruled.

name: Parker, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the court's decision correctly re-establishes the test for state immunity, focusing on whether a judgment directly affects a State's contract or property rights, correcting the misinterpretation from Barnhart.

name: Shaw, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while Barnhart's standard for immunity may have been overbroad, Section 14 can still bar suits against individual state employees if the claims are, in substance, against the State, but that Pinkard's claims do not meet this threshold.

name: Sellers, J.
description: Concurred, argued that while Barnhart's standard for immunity may have been overbroad, Section 14 can still bar suits against individual state employees if the claims are, in substance, against the State, but that Pinkard's claims do not meet this threshold.

name: MITCHELL, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, argued that the trial court correctly dismissed the action based on state immunity, as neither statute cited by claimants imposed a legal duty on the Governor to continue participation in federal unemployment programs.

name: STEWART, JUSTICE
description: Concurred, arguing that the local act and ordinance are constitutional under §§ 89, 104, and 105 of the Alabama Constitution.

name: MENDHEIM, Justice
description: Concurred in the result regarding §§ 89 and 104, but dissented from the main opinion's rationale for upholding the Act under § 105, arguing the "demonstrated local need" exception is nontextual and unworkable.

name: MITCHELL, Justice
description: Concurred in the result but disagreed with the rationale of Part B (§ 105 analysis), arguing that the local act does not cover the same "case" or "matter" as statewide law, and the "local need" exception is unnecessary.

name: PARKER, Chief Justice
description: Dissented, arguing that the Act addresses the same subject as general law and the City failed to demonstrate a specifically local need for red-light cameras, as red-light running is a general statewide danger.

name: BRYAN, Justice
description: Concurred, argued that the Jefferson County Board of Education is an agency of the State and thus entitled to absolute State immunity from suit under Section 14 of the Alabama Constitution, requiring dismissal of the action.

name: MITCHELL, Justice
description: Authored the main opinion, holding the Local Act constitutional as it covers distinct matters from general laws, and further argued that courts should interpret the Alabama Constitution according to its original public meaning.

name: Parker, C.J.
description: Concurred, argued that the term "appropriation" in the main opinion is a generic word for directing tax revenue and should not be interpreted as having bearing on other constitutional challenges.

name: Mendheim, J.
description: Concurred with Part B of the analysis and the result.

name: Shaw, J.
description: Concurred, argued that the Local Act does not conflict with a general law, only a presumption of county commission discretion, which is not prohibited by § 105.

name: Bolin, J.
description: Dissented, concurring with Justice Sellers' argument that the Local Act violates § 105.

name: Sellers, J.
description: Dissented, argued that the Local Act violates § 105 because the matter regulated by the Local Act is already provided for by the general SSUT Act and Budget Control Act.

name: PER CURIAM
description: Concurred, argued that the plain language of the AUPA's definition of "child" excludes unborn children, meaning the alleged father cannot be a presumed father based on prebirth conduct.

name: SELLERS
description: Concurred, but noted concerns that the Act might violate constitutional principles if a biological father's parental rights can be extinguished unilaterally by a mother marrying another man before birth.

name: Bolin
description: Concurred specially with Justice Sellers and concurred in the result of the main opinion.

name: PARKER
description: Concurred in the result, but believed a compelling textual argument could be made that the AUPA's definition of "child" includes unborn children, though such an argument was not adequately presented by the alleged father.

name: Wise
description: Concurred in the result of the main opinion and with Justice Bryan's sentiments.

name: BRYAN
description: Concurred in the result of the main opinion, but agreed with the sentiments expressed by Justice Sellers.

name: SHAW
description: Dissented, argued that the plain language of the AUPA does not exclude an unborn child from the definition of "child" and that the Court of Civil Appeals' decision should not be affirmed.

name: MITCHELL
description: Dissented, argued that the AUPA's definition of "child" includes an unborn child, especially when considering statutory interpretive directions for word tenses, and would remand for a hearing on whether the alleged father met the requirements to claim presumed paternity.

name: MITCHELL, Justice
description: Concurred, arguing that State immunity bars retrospective monetary relief and attorneys lack third-party standing to assert indigent defendants' constitutional rights.

name: Sellers, J.
description: Concurred in the result, arguing that immunity defenses should be resolved before class certification to promote judicial economy and efficiency.
